numberItems.stem: While driving your own car in Oregon, you are convicted of speeding. Under Section 1.4, how soon must you notify your licensing agency (California DMV)?
numberItems.explanation: Section 1.4: notify your licensing agency within 30 days of a conviction in another jurisdiction for any traffic violation except parking, no matter what vehicle you drove (p. 1-16).

numberItems.stem: Your license is revoked. Under Section 1.4 of the handbook, you must notify your employer within:
numberItems.explanation: Section 1.4 says to notify your employer within 2 business days of a suspension, revocation, cancellation or disqualification (p. 1-16); 30 days is for reporting convictions.

numberItems.stem: You hold an H endorsement and are involuntarily committed to a mental health facility. How soon must you notify the state that issued your CDL and surrender the endorsement?
numberItems.explanation: An H holder must notify the issuing state and surrender the HazMat endorsement within 24 hours (p. 1-16).

numberItems.stem: If you do not wear a safety belt and are thrown from the vehicle in a crash, how much more likely are you to be fatally injured?
numberItems.explanation: The handbook says you are 4 times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle without a safety belt (p. 1-16).

numberItems.stem: You are not hauling HazMat. Under the handbook's summary table, a **first** violation of an out-of-service order disqualifies you for at least:
numberItems.explanation: A first out-of-service violation (not HazMat) costs at least 90 days (pp. 1-14, 1-19); 180 days applies when hauling HazMat or 16+ passengers.

numberItems.stem: You violate an out-of-service order for the first time while hauling placarded HazMat. Per the handbook's summary table, you are disqualified for at least:
numberItems.explanation: The summary table gives at least 180 days (up to 2 years) for a first OOS violation while hauling HazMat or 16 or more passengers (p. 1-19).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Your diesel truck (GVWR 30,000 lb) waits at a warehouse, not at a school, and idling is not needed. Under CARB rules, how long may it idle?
options: As long as needed, since only schools are restricted
numberItems.explanation: Commercial diesel vehicles with a GVWR over 10,001 lb are limited to 5 minutes of non-essential idling anywhere in California, and may not idle at all at a school (p. 1-20).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Unless it is exempt, what is the maximum length of a single vehicle?
numberItems.explanation: The maximum length for a single vehicle is 40 ft (p. 1-21); 60 ft is for articulated buses and 65 ft for a tractor with one trailer.

numberItems.stem: [CA] How far may a vehicle's front bumper extend ahead of the fenders, cab or radiator, whichever is foremost?
numberItems.explanation: The front bumper must not extend more than 2 ft ahead of the fenders, cab or radiator (p. 1-21); 3 ft and 4 ft are front load-overhang limits.

numberItems.stem: [CA] What is the maximum length of an articulated bus or trolley coach?
numberItems.explanation: An articulated bus or trolley coach cannot exceed 60 ft (p. 1-21).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Under state law, a truck tractor coupled to one trailer may be at most how long in total?
numberItems.explanation: A truck tractor and trailer combination may not exceed 65 ft total, except as the CVC provides (p. 1-21).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You pull doubles (truck tractor, semitrailer and trailer) within the 75-ft overall limit. How long may each trailer be?
numberItems.explanation: A truck tractor, semitrailer and trailer may be up to 75 ft long, provided neither trailer is longer than 28 ft 6 in (p. 1-21).

numberItems.stem: [CA] If signs are posted, cities and counties may ban combinations longer than how many feet on roads they control?
numberItems.explanation: If posted, cities and counties may prohibit combinations over 60 ft on highways they control (p. 1-21).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Measured from the front of the vehicle or load to the back of the vehicle or load, what is the maximum load length?
numberItems.explanation: The load length on any vehicle or combination may not be more than 75 ft (p. 1-21); 80 ft is only for poles, pipes and similar one-piece loads on approved equipment.

numberItems.stem: [CA] A load of poles rides on a pole dolly pulled by a motor vehicle. How long may this load be?
numberItems.explanation: Loads of only poles, timbers, pipes or single-unit parts may be up to 80 ft long on a pole/pipe dolly, a semitrailer, or a semitrailer plus dolly (p. 1-22).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Your load is made **only of vehicles** (a car carrier). How far may it extend ahead of the front bumper or front tires?
numberItems.explanation: Most loads may extend no more than 3 ft ahead of the front bumper or tires, but a load made solely of vehicles may extend 4 ft (p. 1-22).

numberItems.stem: [CA] On a single vehicle, how far may the load extend to the rear beyond the last point of support?
options: No more than the full length of the wheelbase
No more than 2/3 of the wheelbase
numberItems.explanation: The load may not extend beyond the last point of support more than 2/3 of the wheelbase (p. 1-22).

numberItems.stem: [CA] In feet, what is the maximum width of a vehicle body or its load?
numberItems.explanation: The body or load may not exceed 102 in (8½ ft) (p. 1-22). 8 ft (96 in) is what local roads may post; 9 ft (108 in) is the wheel-to-wheel limit.

numberItems.stem: [CA] For a vehicle on pneumatic (air-filled) tires, what is the maximum width measured from the outside of one wheel to the outside of the opposite wheel?
numberItems.explanation: Wheel-to-wheel width may not exceed 108 in (9 ft) (p. 1-22).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Required devices such as mirrors and lights may extend how far past each side of the vehicle?
numberItems.explanation: Required devices (lights, mirrors and similar) may extend up to 10 in on each side; permitted devices like door handles only 3 in (6 in on one side for recreational vehicles) (p. 1-22).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Cities and counties may post signs on their roads banning vehicles wider than:
numberItems.explanation: Cities and counties may post signs to permit wider vehicles or to prohibit vehicles wider than 96 in (8 ft) (p. 1-22).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You haul loosely piled hay in bulk (not baled). How wide may the load and its racks be?
numberItems.explanation: Loosely piled agricultural products such as hay, straw or legumes: load and racks up to 120 in (p. 1-22).

numberItems.stem: [CA] What is the maximum height of a double-deck bus?
numberItems.explanation: The height limit is 14 ft, except double-deck buses, which may be up to 14 ft 3 in (p. 1-23).

numberItems.stem: [CA] The handbook's single-vehicle axle rule sets a 20,000-lb limit on the wheels at one end of an axle. What is that limit for **buses**?
numberItems.explanation: The wheels at one end of an axle may carry no more than 20,000 lb, or 20,500 lb for buses (p. 1-23).

numberItems.stem: [CA] In a combination with a trailer or semitrailer (using the handbook's listed limits), what is the most the wheels on any one axle may put on the highway?
numberItems.explanation: Any one axle: 18,000 lb; the wheels at one end of an axle: 9,500 lb; a front steering axle may carry up to 12,500 lb (p. 1-23).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Under the combination axle rule, what is the most a front steering axle may carry?
numberItems.explanation: Exception to the 18,000-lb axle limit: the front steering axle may carry up to 12,500 lb (p. 1-23).

numberItems.stem: [CA] An axle group's legal limit is 34,000 lb, and the CHP scale reads 34,250 lb. You haul general freight. What happens?
options: You get a citation and must adjust the load before going on
No citation, because after the 200-lb variation factor you are under the 100-lb standard
You get a citation but may continue, because you are under 1,000 lb over
numberItems.explanation: CHP allows a 200-lb variation factor; only a vehicle still 100 lb or more over after that is cited (p. 1-24). 250 − 200 = 50 lb, so no citation.

numberItems.stem: [CA] A single truck carries livestock and is overweight on an axle group. The driver is cited but may proceed as long as the overage on the axle or axle group is no more than:
numberItems.explanation: Livestock and field-loaded perishables: cited but may proceed if a single truck is no more than 1,000 lb over on any axle or axle group (2,000 lb gross for a combination) (p. 1-24).

numberItems.stem: [CA] For a Motor Carrier Permit (MCP), a motor truck counts as a CMV when it has 2 or more axles and a GVWR over:
numberItems.explanation: The MCP definition includes a motor truck with 2 or more axles weighing more than 10,000 lb GVWR (p. 1-24).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You drive a 2-axle box truck, not towing, on a two-lane undivided highway. No higher limit is posted. What is your maximum speed?
numberItems.explanation: For vehicles not on the 55-mph list, the limit is 65 mph on most highways but 55 mph on 2-lane undivided highways unless a higher limit is posted; 70 only where signed (p. 1-25).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You drive slowly on a two-lane highway where passing is unsafe, and 4 vehicles are lined up behind you. Must you pull into a turnout?
options: Yes, the rule starts at 3 vehicles
Yes, whenever any vehicle is behind you
No, the rule starts at 5 or more vehicles
numberItems.explanation: A slow vehicle must turn out when 5 or more vehicles are behind it on a 2-lane highway where passing is unsafe (p. 1-26).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You drive intrastate hauling **farm products**. You may not drive after being on duty how many hours in any 8 consecutive days?
numberItems.explanation: California intrastate: 80 hours on duty in any 8 consecutive days, or 112 hours when transporting farm products; 70 in 8 is federal (p. 1-27).

numberItems.stem: You drive in **interstate** commerce. Under the handbook's federal hours-of-service table, how many hours may you drive after 10 consecutive hours off duty?
numberItems.explanation: Federal: no more than 11 hours of driving after 10 consecutive hours off duty, and no driving beyond the 14th hour; 12 is the California intrastate limit (p. 1-27).

numberItems.stem: Your truck has a sleeper berth. The required 10 hours off duty may be split into 2 periods if one of them is at least:
numberItems.explanation: With a sleeper berth, the 10 hours may be broken into 2 periods, provided one is not less than 8 hours (p. 1-27).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You drive intrastate and meet adverse weather that was not apparent when the trip began. You may drive 2 extra hours, but never more than how many hours of driving in total?
numberItems.explanation: Adverse weather allows 2 more hours of driving, but in California you may never drive more than 14 hours or after 16 hours on duty (p. 1-27).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You are in a crash in California that injures someone. Within how many days must the SR 1 report reach DMV?
numberItems.explanation: An SR 1 must be submitted to DMV within 10 days for any accident with death, injury or property damage over $1,000 (p. 1-26).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You have a minor crash while driving your employer's truck. Your employer has no special rule. California law says you must tell the employer within:
numberItems.explanation: CVC §16002: notify your employer within 5 days of an accident in the employer's vehicle; the employer may require immediate notice (p. 1-26). 10 days is the SR 1 deadline.

numberItems.stem: [CA] A motor carrier hauls general freight in trucks with a GVWR of 30,000 lb. What is the minimum financial responsibility (combined single limit)?
numberItems.explanation: General freight in vehicles of 10,001 lb GVWR or more: $750,000 CSL; $300,000 is for vehicles of 10,000 lb or less (p. 1-27).

numberItems.stem: [CA] A carrier transports Division 1.1 explosives. What minimum financial responsibility (combined single limit) is required?
numberItems.explanation: Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 explosives, poison gas and similar top-risk loads require a $5,000,000 CSL; oil, HazMat or waste generally $1,000,000 (p. 1-27).

numberItems.stem: A 2-axle truck hauls property in two or more states and does not tow. It must be registered under IRP when its GVW is:
numberItems.explanation: An IRP apportionable vehicle includes one with 2 axles and a GVW over 26,000 lb, 3 or more axles at any weight, or a combination over 26,000 lb (p. 1-29).

numberItems.stem: How does an IFTA licensee file motor fuel tax returns?
options: A separate quarterly return to each state driven in
One yearly return to the base jurisdiction
One quarterly return to the base jurisdiction
numberItems.explanation: The IFTA licensee files one quarterly tax return with the base jurisdiction, which pays the other member jurisdictions (p. 1-28).

numberItems.stem: The IVDR (Driver Trip Report) is the source document for IRP fees and IFTA taxes. How long must the original records be kept?
numberItems.explanation: IVDR original records must be kept for a minimum of 4 years and are subject to audit (p. 1-30).
